title: ai_stream_router plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ai_stream_router` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component AiStreamRouterConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

AiStreamRouterConfig.description: Plugin: ai_stream_router — streaming counterpart to ai_federation. Claims ONLY OpenAI Chat Completions requests with `stream: true` and preserves true end-to-end SSE streaming. Runs at priority 2984 (before ai_semantic_cache at 4057, before ai_federation at 4060). Instead of an internal terminate-and-respond HTTP call, it rewrites the routing decision via RequestContext.route_override_* so the normal proxy dispatch streams the provider response straight back to the client. Strips every canonical client credential header (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, X-API-Key, API-Key, APIKey, X-Goog-Api-Key, X-Access-Token, X-Auth-Token, X-Amz-Security-Token, X-Forwarded-Authorization — case-insensitive and with `_` treated as `-`), the route's own configured authentication header locations, and provider-protocol headers, then injects the provider's credential; gateway-asserted x-consumer-* identity headers are also suppressed toward the provider. openai/openai_compatible providers pass through unchanged except optional stream_options.include_usage injection; anthropic requests are translated to the Anthropic Messages API streaming request and Anthropic SSE events are normalized to OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE. google_gemini requests are translated to the Gemini/streamGenerateContent body shape and provider SSE/JSON streams are normalized to OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE (authentication is the x-goog-api-key header only; Vertex AI OAuth2 is not supported). OpenAI request parameters are mapped exactly or refused with an OpenAI-shaped 400, never silently dropped: response_format (Gemini responseMimeType/responseJsonSchema; refused for Anthropic), n (Gemini candidateCount; n > 1 refused for Anthropic), presence_penalty/frequency_penalty/seed (Gemini; non-zero/any refused for Anthropic), parallel_tool_calls false (Anthropic disable_parallel_tool_use; refused for Gemini with callable tools), and logit_bias/logprobs/top_logprobs (refused for both). Anthropic extended thinking (thinking.type enabled or adaptive) with callable tools or a tool-result continuation is refused because signed thinking blocks cannot round-trip through the OpenAI representation. A strict Gemini json_schema must use only keywords Gemini enforces or it is refused. Gemini thought signatures round-trip through tool_calls[].extra_content.google.thought_signature. Base64 data-URL image_url parts (image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp) in user messages translate to native image parts; remote image URLs are refused. A claimed normalizing 2xx response whose Content-Type is not a supported stream media type fails closed for both translated providers. When it claims a request it sets ctx.metadata ai_stream_router_claimed=true so ai_federation defers. Fails closed by default when a streaming request lacks a top-level string `model` or matches no provider. Non-streaming requests Continue to ai_federation. Provider fallback is NOT implemented and a `fallback` config block is REJECTED at admission (issue #3328): the plugin commits one provider route, credential set, backend TLS resolution, and translated request body before dispatch and never switches providers, pre- or post-first-byte, so a stored fallback policy could only be silently inert. No ai_stream_router.fallback_attempts metadata is emitted. Configuration is strict: unknown root and provider fields are rejected with path-qualified diagnostics (and spelling suggestions when useful), so typos such as `enabeld` cannot silently leave the router enabled. The same constructor contract admits file validate/startup, Admin/database writes, and CP/DP snapshot or reload publication; invalid enabled configs reject publication and retain the last-known-good instance under the plugin's FailClosed policy. NOTE: this plugin is HTTP-only and routes over the normal dispatch path, but the claim commits its own egress policy rather than inheriting the proxy's: an https provider endpoint is verified against the built-in public trust roots only — never the global FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH, never disabled by FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY, and never presenting the global backend client certificate — unless that provider sets inherit_backend_tls: true, and any dns_override inherited from the matched proxy is explicitly revoked so the provider host resolves through provider DNS.

enabled.description: Master switch. When false the plugin never claims requests.

fail_on_missing_model.description: Reject a streaming request that lacks a top-level string `model`. Set to false to pass such requests through (to ai_federation / normal backend).

fail_on_no_matching_provider.description: Reject a streaming request whose `model` matches no configured provider. Set to false to pass such requests through.

inject_usage_options.description: For openai/openai_compatible/azure_openai providers, inject stream_options.include_usage=true so the provider emits a final usage event.

normalize_response_stream.description: Normalize provider-native SSE (e.g. Anthropic Messages API events) to OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE. Disabling forwards provider-native SSE verbatim.

max_stream_bytes.description: Cumulative provider plaintext bytes one Anthropic/Gemini response normalizer accepts before it fails closed with an upstream_error frame. A residual provider Content-Encoding is still decoded under the fixed 8 MiB per-layer residual-decode limit. An explicit null means omission.

max_stream_events.description: Complete provider stream events one Anthropic/Gemini response normalizer accepts before it fails closed. An explicit null means omission.

max_normalized_stream_bytes.description: Cumulative OpenAI-shaped output bytes one Anthropic/Gemini response normalizer may emit before it fails closed. A buffered normalization is additionally bounded by the response's retained ceiling. An explicit null means omission.

providers.description: One or more streaming provider definitions. The first provider (in priority order) whose model_patterns match the request `model` wins.

name.description: Unique provider name (surfaced in ai_stream_router.provider metadata). Must be non-empty, and unique across the instance's providers; that uniqueness check is a runtime admission rule this schema cannot express.

provider_type.description: Provider wire format. openai/openai_compatible/azure_openai pass through (azure_openai authenticates with the api-key header); anthropic and google_gemini are translated + normalized to OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE.

endpoint.description: Full https (or http with allow_plaintext) provider streaming endpoint URL, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions, https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages, or https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent. May contain a literal {model} path placeholder. A google_gemini endpoint without {model} is admitted only when model_patterns is the single exact model name the endpoint path names (.../models/<model>:...), because Gemini routes the model only through the URL. An endpoint query string (e.g. an Azure-style ?api-version=...) is preserved and merged with the client's own query using '&'. Embedded userinfo (user:password@) and a #fragment are rejected. IPv6 literal hosts are bracketed in the forwarded authority.

api_key.description: Provider API key. The resolved value must be a valid HTTP header value (no CR, LF, NUL, or other control byte) or construction fails. Supports a whole-value ${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>} reference resolved from the process environment at construction; a ${...} reference to any other variable, including every other FERRUM_* setting, is refused at admission with a 400. Injected as Authorization: Bearer for openai(-compatible), api-key for azure_openai, x-api-key for anthropic, x-goog-api-key for google_gemini.

model_patterns.description: 1–128 glob patterns matched against the request `model`; each is 1–256 ASCII bytes using letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon, slash, plus, hyphen, or star, with no `..` sequence. `*` is the only wildcard, matches any run of characters except URL-structural separators (`/ ? # & \`) and whitespace, and the pattern is anchored at both ends — so `*mini` matches `model-mini` and `mini-mini` alike, and never matches `mini-pro`. Example: ['gpt-*', 'o*'] or ['claude-*'].

priority.description: Lower = matched first. Defaults to provider index + 1. Stored as a u32, so a larger value is rejected; an explicit null means omission.

allow_plaintext.description: Permit an http:// endpoint. Plaintext provider egress is rejected by default, so this is the required opt-in for an internal HTTP-compatible provider. It has no effect on an https endpoint and does not relax runtime TLS/FIPS policy. An explicit null means omission.

anthropic_version.description: anthropic providers only (a non-null value on any other provider_type is rejected, by this schema and at admission): anthropic-version header value sent to Anthropic providers. Must be a non-empty valid HTTP header value; an explicit null means omission and keeps the default.

default_max_tokens.description: anthropic providers only (a non-null value on any other provider_type is rejected, by this schema and at admission; when omitted on an anthropic provider the router forwards 4096): Anthropic max_tokens forwarded when the OpenAI request sets neither max_tokens nor max_completion_tokens. A present non-null client max_tokens / max_completion_tokens must be a positive integer or the request is rejected with 400. An explicit null means omission.

inherit_backend_tls.description: By default an https provider endpoint is verified against the built-in public trust roots only, isolated from every gateway-global backend TLS fallback: the global FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH is not used, FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY cannot disable verification, and the global backend client certificate (FERRUM_BACKEND_TLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH / _KEY_PATH) is never presented. Set true to keep the proxy's own resolved backend TLS instead — custom CA bundle, SNI/SAN policy, and backend mTLS client certificate, including the gateway-global fallbacks that resolution normally inherits — for internal openai_compatible endpoints behind private PKI. No effect on http endpoints. An explicit null means omission.
